bulbasaur.role: Bulky Grass/Poison special attacker & sleep lead — the easiest solo run in Kanto.
bulbasaur.where: Starter gift from Prof. Oak in Pallet Town — never wild in either version.
bulbasaur.catch: Lv 5 gift. Soft-reset the intro for a good nature/IVs before you commit.
bulbasaur.nature: Modest (+SpA, −Atk) — its whole game is special. Bold/Calm if you want a wall.
bulbasaur.ivs: Special Attack, then Speed, then HP.
bulbasaur.evWhere: Calcium ×10 (Celadon Dept. Store) banks 100 SpA, then KO Gastly in Pokémon Tower; HP Up ×10 for the HP half.
bulbasaur.trainFrom: Lv 16 — the moment it becomes Ivysaur and its bulk turns real.

bulbasaur.notes: No Fairy type in Gen 3, so Poison is clean coverage. Sludge Bomb is post-game — a normal run uses Razor Leaf. TMs are single-use. Frenzy Plant (Cape Brink tutor) recharges a turn and is worse than Giga Drain — skip it.

charmander.role: Fast Fire/Flying mixed attacker — flashy, but fights an uphill Kanto (Rock/Water gyms early).
charmander.where: Starter gift from Prof. Oak in Pallet Town — never wild.
charmander.nature: Modest for a special set; Naive/Hasty if you want Earthquake + Flamethrower mixed.
charmander.ivs: Special Attack and Speed (Modest) — both base 100+ on Charizard.
charmander.evWhere: Calcium ×10 + Carbos ×10; finish SpA on Gastly (Pokémon Tower), Speed in Diglett's Cave.
charmander.trainFrom: Lv 16 as Charmeleon; it leans hard on Prof. Oak's aide Exp. Share early.

charmander.evo: Charmeleon at L16, Charizard at L36 — level-up only.
charmander.notes: Charizard is 2× weak to Rock and Water — the exact types of Brock and Misty, so early game is rough. SpA (109) tops Atk (84); go special unless you commit to the late Earthquake TM. Blast Burn (Cape Brink) recharges — skip.

squirtle.role: Bulky Water tank — the safest starter for a smooth Kanto run.
squirtle.where: Starter gift from Prof. Oak in Pallet Town — never wild.
squirtle.nature: Modest (+SpA) for offense; Bold (+Def) to lean on its excellent bulk.
squirtle.ivs: Special Attack, HP, then the defenses.
squirtle.evs: 252 SpA / 252 HP / 4 SpD (or 252 HP / 252 Def, Bold).
squirtle.evWhere: Calcium/HP Up ×10 each; finish SpA on Gastly (Pokémon Tower), HP off Sevii Marill.

TM26 — Viridian Gym (late)
level 31 / 25 — recovery on a wall build

squirtle.evo: Wartortle at L16, Blastoise at L36 — level-up only.
squirtle.notes: Defenses (100/105) beat its 85 SpA, so it's a tank that hits back, not a sweeper. Hydro Cannon (Cape Brink) recharges — Surf is better. TMs are single-use, but Ice Beam is re-buyable at the Game Corner.

caterpie.role: Turn-one sleep lead — Compound Eyes makes Sleep Powder essentially never miss.
caterpie.where: Wild in Viridian Forest (both versions), plus Routes 24/25.
caterpie.catch: Lv 3–5 in Viridian Forest. Catch rate is trivial.
caterpie.ability: Compound Eyes — boosts accuracy, turning 75%-acc Sleep Powder into ~95%. Its whole reason to exist.
caterpie.evWhere: SpA on Gastly (Pokémon Tower), Speed in Diglett's Cave — both cheap at the levels Butterfree fights.
caterpie.trainFrom: Lv 10 — it evolves almost immediately, so just push to Butterfree.

caterpie.items: Twistedspoon (+10% Psychic) or Silver Powder (+10% Bug).
caterpie.evo: Metapod at L7, Butterfree at L10 — the fastest evolution in the game.
caterpie.final: Lv 30–40; it's an early-game star that fades by the Elite Four.
caterpie.notes: Frail (60/50/50 defenses) and outclassed lategame, but the free, reliable sleep it gives your whole team through the mid-game is worth the slot. Bug/Flying is 4× weak to Rock.

weedle.role: Early physical stinger — fine while the game is young, drop it by the mid-game.
weedle.where: Wild in Viridian Forest (LeafGreen) / Routes 24-25; sparse in FireRed's forest.
weedle.ability: Swarm (its only ability) — boosts Bug moves at low HP.
weedle.evWhere: Attack off Mankey/Nidoran on the early routes; Speed in Diglett's Cave.
weedle.trainFrom: Lv 10 — evolves as fast as Caterpie.

weedle.items: Silver Powder (+10% Bug) or Poison Barb.
weedle.evo: Kakuna at L7, Beedrill at L10.
weedle.final: Lv 25–35; honestly a bench player after the first few badges.
weedle.notes: Beedrill's 80 Atk / 75 Spe and shallow movepool age badly, and Bug/Poison is a poor defensive type. Great early pick-up, not an endgame keeper. There is no Swords Dance tutor in FR/LG to prop it up.

nidoran-m.notes: Moon Stones aren't sold — save one. Its EQ + Ice Beam + Thunderbolt coverage answers most of Kanto; the only catch is Earthquake arriving late, so it plays as a special attacker (Ice Beam/Thunderbolt) until then.

diglett.nature: Jolly (+Spe) — you want to out-speed everything and hit first.
diglett.ability: Arena Trap (prefer — the foe can't switch out) over Sand Veil. Random on catch.
